question: How many countries will abstain on the IAEA General Conference resolution 'Application of IAEA safeguards in the Middle East' at the 70th General Conference?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: recorded whole-resolution votes on the annual Egyptian-tabled 'Application of IAEA Safeguards in the Middle East' resolution at the IAEA GC, which has gone to a vote rather than consensus since ~2006. The abstention column is a narrow, stable Western-aligned bloc (Israel, US, Canada plus a handful of others), giving 7-8-9-7 across 2022-2025 (mean 7.75, no trend). I verified 112-0-9 for GC68/2024 and 120 in favour for GC69/2025 from independent secondary reporting; primary IAEA PDFs were fetch-blocked (402/403). Key evidence against a large shift: 2025 came AFTER the June 2025 strikes on Iranian nuclear sites and still fell back to the low end (7), so the bloc appears insensitive to regional escalation. Upside mechanism: if Egypt hardens the 2026 text (e.g. attack-condemnation language, as in the contested 2025 physical-protection text), additional EU states could abstain, which is the plausible route to 10+. Downside mechanism: the US or Israel switching abstain->against subtracts from this column. No prediction market exists on any venue, so no crowd anchor. I could not retrieve 2017-2021 tallies despite repeated searches, so my dispersion rests on only four observations and I widened accordingly rather than trusting the n=4 SD. Separate annulment risk (consensus adoption, ~5-8%) does not shift these conditional percentiles. p_above_upper=0.02 prices an en-masse EU abstention past 15.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: Resolves off the abstentions figure (third number) in the recorded roll-call vote on the resolution AS A WHOLE, expected symbol GC(70)/RES/xx, published under the IAEA General Conference documents for the 70th session. NOT the separate vote sometimes taken on operative paragraph 2 alone, and NOT the distinct 'Israeli Nuclear Capabilities' resolution. If the whole resolution is adopted by consensus with no abstention count recorded, or the item is deferred, the question is annulled.

EVENT WINDOW: 14 September 2026 -> 18 September 2026 per the 70th regular session dates in the criteria; the Middle East safeguards item is customarily taken up and voted 17-18 September. As of Now (2026-09-07T21:35Z) 0% of the event window has elapsed; the session opens in ~7 days.

EVIDENCE BULLETS:
- The 70th regular session of the IAEA General Conference is scheduled 14-18 September 2026 at the Vienna International Centre (IAEA GC70 page, retrieved 2026-09-07).
- 2025, GC(69)/RES/15: adopted with 120 in favour, 0 against, 7 abstentions. The 120-in-favour figure is independently confirmed by Jordan Pulse reporting on Egypt's resolution at the 69th GC.
- 2024, GC(68)/RES/14: 112 in favour, 0 against, 9 abstentions. Egypt Today reported the 68th session adopted Egypt's draft with 112 in favour, none against, nine abstaining.
- 2023, GC(67)/RES/13: 115 in favour, 0 against, 8 abstentions.
- 2022, GC(66)/RES/12: 117 in favour, 0 against, 7 abstentions.
- 2019, GC(63)/RES/13: operative paragraph 2 was put to a SEPARATE recorded vote and approved 117-1-10. This is a different instrument from the whole-resolution vote and would not resolve this question, but it indicates the magnitude of the dissenting bloc in that year.
- The resolution has not been adopted by consensus since approximately 2006; Israel, the United States, Canada, and at times some EU states have been the states declining to vote in favour (secondary sourcing via search index, 2026-09-07).
- The Arms Control Association 'WMD-Free Middle East Proposal at a Glance' factsheet (fetched 2026-09-07) describes the resolution only as adopted annually 'without objections' since 1991 and gives NO year-by-year tallies; it does not distinguish consensus adoption from a 0-against recorded vote, so it should not be read as evidence about the abstention column.
- Regional context carried into 2026: the June 2025 attacks on Iranian nuclear sites and facilities were the subject of a separately contested GC text at the 69th session that 'strongly condemned' them; Israel's representative placed on record deep concerns over the 'non-consensual and politically motivated' Middle East text adopted at that session.
- The 2025 session (7 abstentions) occurred after those June 2025 strikes, i.e. the most recent observation was taken under a highly escalated regional environment.
- The 2024 session (9 abstentions) was the high mark of the recent series and coincided with peak Gaza-war-related diplomatic tension at the Agency.
- IAEA membership has grown to roughly 180 states, so the denominator of possible abstainers drifts slowly upward over time; total votes cast varied 112-120 across 2022-2025, indicating attendance at the moment of the vote itself fluctuates by several states year to year.

BASE RATES:
- Over all four most recent sessions with a recorded whole-resolution vote (2022-2025): abstentions were 7, 8, 9, 7 — mean 7.75, median 7.5, range 7-9, SD 0.96, no monotone trend (year-over-year changes +1, +1, -2). Source: question background, with 2024 and 2025 independently corroborated as above.
- Conditional on the resolution going to a recorded vote at all (the condition this question requires to resolve): every session 2022-2025 met this condition, i.e. 4 of 4.
- Over the same four sessions, votes AGAINST were 0 in every case, so the abstention column has been the sole repository of non-affirmative positions.
- Component composition of the abstention column (over the recent period): a persistent core of Israel, the United States and Canada, plus a variable remainder of roughly four to six additional Western-aligned or small states; the year-to-year variation comes from that variable remainder and from which of them are present in the hall, not from the core.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: Egypt tables the same text, it goes to a roll-call vote late in the session, it passes with zero against, and the abstention column lands within the band it has occupied in each of the last four sessions.

EVIDENCE POINTING TOWARD A HIGHER COUNT: membership and attendance drift upward; a hardened 2026 text (for example incorporating attack-condemnation language of the kind that proved contentious at the 69th session) would be the recognised mechanism by which additional European states move from 'in favour' to 'abstain'; 2024 demonstrates the column can move up by two in a single year under diplomatic strain.
EVIDENCE POINTING TOWARD A LOWER COUNT: 2025 reverted to the bottom of the band despite maximal regional escalation; a shift by the United States or Israel from 'abstain' to 'against' would move states out of the abstention column entirely and has become more conceivable given more assertive stated positions on 'non-consensual and politically motivated' Middle East texts; the 2025 session drew the largest in-favour total of the four, consistent with a narrowing rather than widening dissent bloc.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: (a) the GC(70)/1 provisional agenda or any GC70 draft resolution text confirming the item is tabled for 2026 — nothing published or indexed as of 2026-09-07; (b) the named list of abstaining states for any of 2022-2025 — no source retrieved gives the roster; (c) whole-resolution tallies for 2017-2021 (GC61-GC65), so the series here is only four points long; (d) any prediction market on any venue pricing this quantity. Primary IAEA PDFs (gc69resdec-2025.pdf, gc69-or9.pdf, gc63-res13.pdf, the GC70 landing page) returned HTTP 402/403 to dir

calls.reasoning: Prior from the four most recent recorded votes on this exact resolution as a whole: 7, 8, 9, 7 abstentions (mean 7.75), against total ballots of 124/123/121/127. The text is essentially unchanged boilerplate Egypt has tabled since the 1990s, and the abstainer set (Israel plus a handful of Western/US-aligned and small Pacific states) is structurally sticky, so the status-quo outcome is another single-digit count near 8. I widened well beyond the raw 4-observation SD because n=4 understates the process variance: attendance alone swung ~6 ballots across those sessions, and 2026 carries live regional conflict plus a US administration pressing allies on Israel-related multilateral texts, which could add a couple of abstainers; pulling the other way, 2025 delivered the largest in-favour total and joint-lowest abstention count, implying strong Arab/NAM mobilization. Evidence is thin and one-sided in the sense that no GC(70) draft or attendance signal exists yet, so I stayed close to the base rate rather than reading the conflict news into a shift. No market exists (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers: none found). Escape above 15 priced at 2% for the concrete mechanism of a toughened 2026 text (e.g. language on attacks on safeguarded facilities) triggering a coordinated EU/Western bloc abstention.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION AND INSTRUMENT
- Resolution 'Application of IAEA safeguards in the Middle East' is tabled annually by Egypt on behalf of the Arab Group and put to a recorded (roll-call) vote; recent symbols GC(66)/RES/12 (2022), GC(67)/RES/13 (2023), GC(68)/RES/14 (2024), GC(69)/RES/15 (2025) [IAEA GC resolution series].
- Resolution-instrument note: the figure at issue is recorded on the resolution AS A WHOLE, in the GC(70) resolution document footnote and the GC(70)/OR record of proceedings. It resolves off that, NOT off the separate vote on operative paragraph 2, and NOT off news summaries that report only 'X countries voted in favour'.
- Adoption by consensus with no abstention count recorded would annul the question; the item was put to a recorded vote in each of the last four sessions.

EVENT WINDOW
- Event window: 2026-09-14 -> 2026-09-18 per the criteria (70th regular session, Vienna International Centre); the Middle East item is customarily taken up and voted 17-18 September. As of 2026-09-07T21:35Z, 0% elapsed - the session has not opened.

RECORDED VOTES (in favour - against - abstentions)
- Whole resolution: 2022: 117-0-7; 2023: 115-0-8; 2024: 112-0-9; 2025: 120-0-7 [question background; the 2022 figure appears in the GC(66)/RES/12 document text, and Egypt Today (19 Sep 2025) independently reports 120 in favour in 2025].
- Total ballots cast (favour+against+abstain) in those four sessions: 124, 123, 121, 127 - participation moves by ~6 votes year to year against roughly 180 member states.
- Separate OP2 votes, a DIFFERENT and more contested instrument that does not count here: 2019: 117-1-10; 2022: 115-1-9; 2023: 114-1-11; 2024: 112-1-7 [IAEA GC(63)/RES/13, GC(66)/RES/12, GC(67)/RES/13, GC(68)/RES/14 document texts].

BASE RATES BY CLASS
- Over the four most recent whole-resolution roll-calls (2022-2025): abstentions 7, 8, 9, 7 - mean 7.75, observed spread 2.
- Over the four most recent OP2 separate votes (different class): abstentions 10, 9, 11, 7 - mean 9.25.
- Conditional on participation: in the two higher-turnout sessions (124 and 127 ballots) abstentions were 7 and 7; in the two lower-turnout sessions (123 and 121 ballots) they were 8 and 9.

COMPOSITION AND TEXT STABILITY
- Abstainers have historically comprised Israel plus Western/US-aligned states (United States, Canada, Australia among those named) and some small Pacific delegations; the exact set varies with attendance and diplomatic positioning. Israel has repeatedly placed on record its objection to the 'non-consensual and politically motivated' Middle East text.
- The Egyptian text is substantively carried forward from the 1990s series (GC(39)/RES/24 of 22 Sep 1995 onward) [FAS MENWFZ document collection].
- The separate, far more contested 'Israeli nuclear capabilities' resolution has not been tabled for a vote since 2013, when it was defeated 43-51-32 [Arms Control Association, Oct 2013]; the safeguards text is the surviving vehicle.

2026 CONTEXT (BOTH DIRECTIONS)
- The IAEA Board of Governors adopted a resolution urging Iran to cooperate on 10 June 2026; DG Grossi's March and June 2026 Board statements address the impact of regional conflict on nuclear safety and safeguards in Iran. Regional conflict is live going into GC(70).
- Pressure toward a larger abstaining bloc: Western/US alignment with Israel amid the 2025-26 conflict, and a US administration that has pressed allies on Israel-related multilateral texts.
- Pressure toward a smaller one: the 2025 session produced the highest in-favour total of the four and the joint-lowest abstention count, indicating strong Arab/NAM mobilization on this specific text.

SEARCHED FOR BUT NOT FOUND
- Any published GC(70) draft resolution text, supplementary agenda item list, or provisional voting schedule.
- Whole-resolution abstention counts for GC(63)-GC(65) (2019-2021).
- The named 2025 abstainer list: GC(69)/OR.9 could not be retrieved (iaea.org returned HTTP 402 to the fetch tool; direct download was blocked).
- Any prediction market or bookmaker contract on this quantity: Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi and bookmakers - none found.
- The Journal for Peace and Nuclear Disarmament article on the ME WMDFZ in the IAEA GC, which may contain a longer vote table, returned HTTP 403 and was not read.

calls.reasoning: Base rate first: the seven most recent recorded votes on this exact resolution gave abstentions of 11, 8, 7, 7, 8, 9, 7 (mean 8.1, median 8, SD 1.46); the last six are tightly bunched 7-9. The abstaining bloc is structural and small: Israel and the USA are near-locks, joined recently by pro-Israel-aligned Latin American governments (Argentina, Paraguay, El Salvador in 2025) plus attendance-dependent one-offs (Georgia, Togo in 2025; India, Nepal, Uganda, Tanzania appear on the separate paragraph-2 vote but not on the whole text). Year-to-year variation is driven mostly by which small delegations are in the room and by marginal Western repositioning, not by regional events - notably the September 2025 vote came three months after the June 2025 Israeli/US strikes on Iran and produced the LOWEST recent abstention count (7) with the HIGHEST yes count (120), so escalation did not mechanically push abstentions up. Countervailing: the pro-Israel-aligned bloc has been growing, GC70 will also take up Iran's deferred 'prohibition of armed attack against nuclear facilities' draft, and 2019 shows 11 is reachable, so the upper tail is fatter than the lower one (the floor is bounded near the hard core of ~5-6 committed abstainers). I centre just below 8 with mass concentrated on 7-9 and an asymmetric right tail; 2% priced above the open upper bound for a discontinuous realignment (large EU/Western bloc shifting to abstention on a contested amended text). No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers - zero external anchor, so this is pure reference-class work.

SUBJECT: abstention count on the IAEA GC resolution 'Application of IAEA Safeguards in the Middle East' at GC(70), 14-18 Sept 2026.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the abstentions figure (third number) in the footnote of the adopted resolution document GC(70)/RES/xx published on iaea.org, NOT off the separate recorded vote on operative paragraph 2, and NOT off the companion 'Israeli nuclear capabilities' item. Adoption without a recorded vote (consensus), deferral, or no vote = annulled.

EVENT WINDOW: 14 Sept 2026 -> 18 Sept 2026 per the resolution criteria (70th regular session). As of Now = 2026-09-07T21:35Z the session has not opened: 0% of the window elapsed, ~6.1 days to opening. In past sessions this item was taken near the end: adopted 19 Sept 2019, 24 Sept 2020, 22 Sept 2021 (11th plenary), 29 Sept 2022, 28 Sept 2023, 19 Sept 2024, 18 Sept 2025 (8th plenary).

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: Egypt/Arab Group table the text annually; it goes to a roll-call vote and is adopted with zero votes against and a single-digit number of abstentions.

BASE RATES - class: recorded vote on THIS resolution as a whole, GC(63) 2019 through GC(69) 2025, n=7 (source: the individual IAEA resolution PDFs, footnote 1 of each):
- 2019 GC(63)/RES/13: 117 / 0 / 11
- 2020 GC(64)/RES/15: 111 / 0 / 8
- 2021 GC(65)/RES/14: 113 / 0 / 7
- 2022 GC(66)/RES/12: 117 / 0 / 7
- 2023 GC(67)/RES/13: 115 / 0 / 8
- 2024 GC(68)/RES/14: 112 / 0 / 9
- 2025 GC(69)/RES/15: 120 / 0 / 7
Mean 8.14, median 8, sample SD 1.46, range 7-11. Sub-class conditioned on the six post-2019 sessions only: mean 7.67, range 7-9.
Total ballots cast (yes+abstain, no 'against' in any year): 128, 119, 120, 124, 123, 121, 127 - i.e. turnout among ~180 members varies by up to 9 delegations year to year, which is itself a driver of the abstention count.

COMPOSITION (source: GC(69)/OR.8, 8th plenary, 18 Sept 2025):
- Abstained on the resolution AS A WHOLE (7): Argentina, El Salvador, Georgia, Israel, Paraguay, Togo, United States of America.
- Separate roll-call on operative paragraph 2 the same day: 117 in favour, 1 against (Israel), 9 abstaining - Argentina, El Salvador, Georgia, India, Nepal, Paraguay, Uganda, United Republic of Tanzania, United States. Note the two abstainer sets differ; the paragraph-2 set is excluded by the fine print.
- Canada does not appear in the 2025 whole-resolution abstainer list despite being named as a historical abstainer in general commentary.

EVIDENCE POINTING BOTH WAYS:
- Upward: the 2025 abstainer set includes three Latin American governments (Argentina, Paraguay, El Salvador) whose current administrations are strongly Israel-aligned, a bloc that was smaller earlier in the series; 2019 shows 11 is attainable; Iran withdrew its draft on 'Prohibition of armed attacks against nuclear installations' at GC(69) and its co-sponsors said they would defer action to the next General Conference (GC(69)/OR.9), so GC(70) faces an additional contested Middle East item that could harden positions.
- Downward/stabilising: GC(69) in Sept 2025 came three months after the June 2025 Israeli and US strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities and produced the highest yes count (120) and the joint-lowest abstention count (7) of the series - regional escalation did not translate into more abstentions; several 2025 abstainers (Togo, Georgia, El Salvador) are small delegations whose presence in the room varies; the resolution text is largely rolled over year to year.
- Institutional calendar: IAEA Board of Governors met 7-11 September 2026 (the week containing Now); GC(70) documents in the gc70-XX series are being published (e.g. GC(70)/10, DG report on nuclear and radiation safety). GC(70) runs 14-18 Sept 2026 at the Vienna International Centre.

calls.reference_class: Recorded roll-call votes on the annual IAEA General Conference resolution 'Application of IAEA safeguards in the Middle East', sessions GC(63) 2019 through GC(69) 2025 (n=7)

calls.reasoning: Seven-session series of abstentions: 11, 8, 7, 7, 8, 9, 7 (mean 8.1, median 8, SD 1.46), with zero votes against in every year. The abstaining bloc is structural but thin: the named 2025 roster from GC(69)/OR.8 is Israel, USA, Argentina, Paraguay, El Salvador, Georgia, Togo — only two or three hard locks, the rest attendance-dependent or newly Israel-aligned. Regional escalation does not drive this number: GC(69) met three months after the June 2025 strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities and produced the highest in-favour count (120) and joint-lowest abstentions (7) of the series. I centre just under 8 with mass concentrated on 7-9, a fatter right tail (the growing Israel-aligned Latin American bloc, a possible hardened 2026 text, 2019 showing 11 is reachable) and a modestly softer low side than the individual runs allowed, since the corrected roster shows the floor is not anchored by a large permanent core. No GC(70) draft text, agenda or sponsor list is published as of 2026-09-07, so there is no 2026-specific signal to update on.
calls.reconciliation: Two factual disputes and two judgment calls. FACTUAL 1 - series length: Runs 1 and 2 had only 2022-2025 (n=4) after IAEA PDFs returned 402/403; Run 3 retrieved the GC(63)-GC(69) footnotes giving 11,8,7,7,8,9,7. Run 3's 2022-2025 values match the other two exactly, corroborating it where it overlaps, so I adopt n=7. Residual unsettled point: Run 3's 2019 whole-resolution tally (117-0-11) shares its in-favour count with the 2019 OP2 vote (117-1-10) that Runs 1 and 2 both cite, so conflation cannot be excluded without web access; I let it carry that uncertainty by treating 11 as a tail data point rather than a firm anchor. FACTUAL 2 - abstainer composition: Runs 1 and 2 name Canada as a persistent core abstainer from general commentary; Run 3 cites the GC(69)/OR.8 plenary record listing the seven 2025 abstainers (Argentina, El Salvador, Georgia, Israel, Paraguay, Togo, USA) with Canada absent. A named plenary record beats commentary, so Run 3 settles it — and it changes the shape: only ~2-3 locks, the rest swing delegations, which widens my low tail relative to all three runs. JUDGMENT 1 - does 2026 escalation raise the count: all runs supply the same decisive datum (Sept 2025 vote, post-June-2025 strikes, produced the LOWEST abstentions and HIGHEST yes of the series), so no upward adjustment. JUDGMENT 2 - drift direction: the newly Israel-aligned Latin American bloc argues up, the most recent observation of 7 and rolled-over text argue down; no evidence breaks this tie, so I placed the asymmetry in the right tail and set the median at the 7/8 boundary rather than shading the centre. I carry Run 3's reference class forward because it is the longest correctly-scoped one, and set dispersion from its SD widened for skew and turnout. No web access this run; sources is empty by design. Market check: no contract on any venue per the harness search and all three runs — no crowd anchor to blend.

disagreements.claim: The base-rate series is 4 sessions (2022-2025) vs 7 sessions (2019-2025, including 11 abstentions in 2019)
disagreements.verdict: Settled toward Run 3: it retrieved the primary footnotes past the fetch blocks that stopped Runs 1-2, and its overlapping 2022-2025 values match theirs exactly. Adopted n=7, mean 8.14, SD 1.46.

disagreements.claim: Run 3's 2019 whole-resolution figure of 117-0-11 may be the separate OP2 vote (117-1-10) mis-attributed — the in-favour counts coincide
disagreements.verdict: Could NOT be settled without web access. Treated as a soft tail data point rather than a hard anchor; it fattens the right tail modestly but does not move the centre.

disagreements.claim: Canada is a persistent core abstainer on the whole resolution
disagreements.verdict: Settled against Runs 1-2. GC(69)/OR.8 names the 2025 abstainers as Argentina, El Salvador, Georgia, Israel, Paraguay, Togo, USA — no Canada. A named plenary record outweighs unsourced commentary; this shrinks the assumed hard core and widens the low tail.

disagreements.claim: 2025-26 regional conflict and US pressure on allies should push abstentions above the base rate
disagreements.verdict: Resolved on shared evidence, not by fiat: GC(69) sat three months after the June 2025 strikes and returned the joint-lowest abstention count (7) with the highest in-favour (120). No upward shift applied for escalation.

disagreements.claim: Whether the central estimate should sit at 7 (most recent, modal) or near 8 (series mean, growing Israel-aligned bloc)
disagreements.verdict: Pure judgment, no evidence breaks it. I took the reading I would bet on: median 7.9 — mass concentrated on 7-9 with the mode at 7, the asymmetry expressed in the right tail rather than by dragging the centre up.

disagreements.verdict: Settled: all three runs plus the harness title search found no contract on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers. None found — no crowd anchor.
